task_summary: I am an integration tester. I need to design integration tests for the user registration functionality. Before defining the tests, I need to understand the high-level architecture supporting this functionality. I want to identify the main components involved in the registration process, their responsibilities, and the interactions and dependencies among them. In particular, I need to understand which components handle the registration request, validate the user's personal information and selected role, manage role-specific data such as the student ID or librarian identifier, verify the validity and uniqueness of the account, and persist the newly created user. I also need to understand how these components collaborate when invalid or already existing user data is provided, so that I can identify the main integration points and interactions that should be covered by the tests. | design integration tests | user registration functionality | The diagram must make clear the high-level architecture, main components, their responsibilities, interactions, dependencies, and collaboration when handling valid, invalid, or already existing user data for the registration process.

architectural_questions.text: Which components are responsible for handling the user registration functionality and validating personal information, selected roles, and unique account data?
What is the exact order of calls and execution flow among components when the user registration functionality processes valid, invalid, or already existing user data?
What are the specific interactions and communication pathways between the components involved in the user registration functionality?
Which modules or classes own the persistence and role-specific data management logic for the user registration functionality?
